paper_claim: Appendix D presents 210 'theorem-level' stress tests that allegedly converge on life-first.

tests.title: Gödel’s Incompleteness (meta-logic)
tests.note: Gödel's incompleteness is about formal systems; it does not imply an ethical axiom. The 'necessary meta-axiom' conclusion is a non sequitur.

tests.title: Cantor’s Diagonalization (lists can’t close the set)
tests.note: Diagonalization shows that certain lists cannot exhaust a set; it does not show that value lists collapse without life.

tests.title: Modal Logic (necessity vs. possibility)
tests.note: Box(V -> Life) is asserted, not proved. Even if true, it establishes necessity, not lexical priority.

tests.title: Decision Theory / Expected Utility
tests.note: Setting u(death)=0 is a modeling choice. Expected utility does not entail a lexicographic life constraint.

tests.title: Game Theory / Nash Stability
tests.note: Life-preserving strategies are not the only Nash equilibria; payoffs, institutions, and information determine equilibria.

tests.title: Information Theory (signal, entropy, meaning)
tests.note: Semantic truth is not identical to channel capacity. 'No decoder' does not make truth claims meaningless in the relevant sense.

tests.title: Evolutionary Game Theory / Replicator Dynamics
tests.note: Anti-life strategies can persist; 'self-negating' is not a general evolutionary result.

tests.title: Thermodynamics / Far-from-equilibrium Systems
tests.note: Life is not the only far-from-equilibrium structure; a thermodynamic fact does not yield a moral priority.

tests.title: Pascal’s Wager / Risk Dominance
tests.note: Risk dominance can be a decision heuristic, but the probabilities and utilities are unspecified. It is not a proof.

tests.title: Fixed-Point Theorems (stability under iteration)
tests.note: No contraction mapping or function is defined. 'Life-first is the only non-degenerate fixed point' is asserted.

tests.title: Cooperation Theorems / Repeated Prisoner’s Dilemma
tests.note: Cooperation can be rational in repeated games, but the specific life-first norm does not follow; other equilibria exist.

tests.title: Kolmogorov Complexity / Minimum Description Length
tests.note: Simplicity is not truth. 'Life-first' is not shown to be the shortest description of morality.

tests.title: Tarski’s Undefinability of Truth (meta-levels again)
tests.note: Tarski's undefinability theorem concerns truth predicates in formal languages; it does not imply a moral axiom.

tests.title: Catastrophe Theory / Tipping Points
tests.note: Tipping points are real, but the normative conclusion is not derived from catastrophe theory.

tests.title: Moral Philosophy Triangulation (Kant, Utilitarianism, Virtue)
tests.note: Kantian, utilitarian, and virtue frameworks all presuppose agents, but they disagree about priority. Convergence is asserted, not shown.

tests.title: Bayes’ Theorem (evidence aggregation)
tests.note: The likelihoods are not estimated. 'Posterior near 1' is a rhetorical assertion, not a Bayesian result.

tests.title: No Free Lunch Theorem (optimization limits)
tests.note: No free lunch concerns optimization algorithms; it does not imply a universal moral constraint.

tests.title: Arrow’s Impossibility Theorem (voting paradoxes)
tests.note: Arrow's theorem concerns social-choice aggregation. A lexicographic life-first rule may violate other fairness conditions and is not a resolution.

tests.title: Second Law of Thermodynamics (entropy growth)
tests.note: Entropy is not a moral measure. The second law does not rank values.

tests.title: Survivorship Bias (hidden failures)
tests.note: The fact that we can argue does not show that life-first strategies are uniquely survivable.

tests.title: Reductio ad Absurdum (proof by contradiction)
tests.note: Assuming 'something else is most important' and then assuming life ends does not produce a contradiction unless one assumes life is necessary for meaning.

tests.title: Black Swan Theory (rare catastrophic events)
tests.note: Precaution is reasonable under uncertainty, but it does not establish the specific principle or its scope.

tests.title: Precautionary Principle (burden of proof under risk)
tests.note: The precautionary principle supports caution; it can also justify arbitrary restrictions. It is not a lexicographic proof.

tests.title: Kant’s Universalizability (categorical imperative)
tests.note: Universalizability tests maxims, not the ranking of life over every other value.

tests.title: Sigma (Σ) Collapse of Values
tests.note: If values are modeled as zero without life, the sum is zero. That is a modeling assumption, not an argument for priority.

tests.title: Set Theory / Support Non-Emptiness
tests.note: Values are not functions requiring a nonempty support set in the relevant sense.

tests.title: Order Theory / Lexicographic Priority
tests.note: One can define a lexicographic order, but the choice of order is normative and needs argument.

tests.title: Measure Theory / Absolute Continuity of Value on Life
tests.note: 'Value measure' is undefined; absolute continuity is a modeling choice, not a moral result.

tests.title: Category Theory (Arrows Require Objects)
tests.note: Moral values are not objects and morphisms. The category-theory analogy is decorative.

tests.title: Temporal Logic (LTL/CTL) Safety Invariant
tests.note: G(Life>0) is a safety invariant if specified, but it does not establish that life outranks all other values.

tests.title: Deontic Logic (Obligation Semantics)
tests.note: Obligations presuppose agents, but not that life protection is the ground of all obligations.

tests.title: Epistemic Logic / Common Knowledge
tests.note: Knowledge requires agents; that does not establish a moral ranking.

tests.title: Causal Inference (do-Calculus)
tests.note: Interventions and counterfactuals are formal tools; they do not yield a moral target.

tests.title: Counterfactuals (Structural Causal Models)
tests.note: Counterfactual value may require subjects, but that is a contested metaethical premise.

tests.title: Program Verification / Invariant Proofs
tests.note: Invariants are useful in program verification, but 'life=0' is not a program state.

tests.title: Model Checking (Automata over Policies)
tests.note: Model checking can verify temporal properties, but the moral target is not a finite-state model.

tests.title: Type Theory / Curry–Howard (Lightweight Analogy)
tests.note: Curry-Howard does not ground moral value.

tests.title: Robust Control (H-∞ / Worst-Case Design)
tests.note: Worst-case control design is useful, but the analogy to ethics is not a proof.

tests.title: Control Barrier Certificates
tests.note: A control barrier requires dynamics and a safe set; 'life>0' is not specified as one.

tests.title: Viability Theory (Aubin)
tests.note: Viability kernels are formal; the moral conclusion is not derived.

tests.title: Risk Measures (CVaR / Tail Risk)
tests.note: Tail risk is relevant, but extinction is not a quantified random variable in the paper.

tests.title: Maximin (Rawlsian Security)
tests.note: Maximin is a decision rule under uncertainty, not a proof of life's priority.

tests.title: Minimax Regret
tests.note: Minimax regret is a decision rule; it does not entail a lexicographic life constraint.

tests.title: Multi-Objective Optimization / Pareto & ε-Constraint
tests.note: Epsilon-constraints are a modeling choice. Life as a hard constraint is asserted, not derived.

tests.title: Mechanism Design / Incentive Compatibility
tests.note: Incentive compatibility does not imply life-first.

tests.title: Survival Analysis (Hazard Functions)
tests.note: Hazard functions are a tool; 'life-first' is not a hazard model.

tests.title: Markov Chains / Absorbing States
tests.note: Absorbing states are real, but the moral conclusion is not derived.

tests.title: Reliability Engineering / Fault-Tree Top Event

tests.title: Percolation Theory / Network Robustness

tests.note: Contracts require parties; they do not require life-first.

tests.title: Moral Uncertainty “Parliament” Models

tests.title: Aumann Agreement Theorem (common priors, rationality)
tests.note: Aumann's theorem requires common priors and honest updating; it does not imply convergence on life-first.

tests.title: Legal Strict Scrutiny Analogy
tests.note: Strict scrutiny is a legal analogy; 'life' is not a legal right in the relevant sense.

tests.title: Systems Engineering “V-Model” (Top Requirement)
